stem: An adult client with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and moderate hepatic impairment has an order to start argatroban at the usual initial infusion rate used for HIT in clients without hepatic impairment. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Question the order because hepatic impairment substantially reduces argatroban clearance and current labeling recommends a lower initial dose with close aPTT-guided titration
options.B: Administer the usual initial infusion because argatroban is eliminated primarily by the kidneys and hepatic impairment does not affect exposure
options.C: Replace argatroban with unfractionated heparin because heparin is preferred when HIT has already been diagnosed
options.D: Administer argatroban without coagulation monitoring because direct thrombin inhibitors do not require laboratory titration in HIT

rationale: Argatroban is an approved nonheparin anticoagulant for adult HIT. In moderate or severe hepatic impairment, clearance is markedly reduced and current labeling recommends a lower initial infusion with careful aPTT monitoring and titration. For HIT, aPTT is used to monitor therapy. Heparin should not be restarted simply because hepatic impairment is present.
educational_objective: Recognize hepatic impairment as a major argatroban dosing and monitoring consideration in HIT.
source_locator: Sections 1.1, 2.2, 2.4 and 8.6 — HIT indication; aPTT monitoring; reduced initial dose in moderate/severe hepatic impairment due to decreased clearance
source_claim_supported: Argatroban is indicated for adult HIT; hepatic impairment requires lower starting dose and careful aPTT titration.

correction_summary: Replaced direct-thrombin-inhibitor recall with an order-safety scenario using the 2026 hepatic-impairment dosing warning and aPTT monitoring requirement. Avoided the unsupported source phrase about antibody cross-reactivity as the main nursing decision point.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.claim_by_claim: HIT indication, hepatic clearance reduction, lower initial dosing and aPTT monitoring are explicit.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; argatroban clearance is reduced in hepatic impairment.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; HIT precludes routine heparin reuse.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; aPTT monitoring guides HIT therapy.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A addresses the labeled hepatic dosing issue.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked renal function, hepatic severity, PCI versus HIT monitoring and warfarin transition; no unresolved conflict.
